stem: Six persons P, Q, R, S, T and U are sitting in a straight row facing north. P sits third from the left. Q sits to the immediate right of P. R sits at one of the ends. U sits to the immediate left of R. T sits between S and U. S is not adjacent to R. Who sits second from the right?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Omitting the 'T between S and U' constraint and placing T at position 5 gives an invalid arrangement.
Reading 'U immediately left of R' as 'U immediately right of R' shifts U to position 6 and places S at position 5.
Placing Q at position 4 and then solving for second from left rather than second from right yields Q as the answer.

R at an end with U immediately left: R=6, U=5. P=3, Q=4. Remaining positions 1 and 2 for S and T. T between S and U means S < T < U positionally, so S=1, T=2. S(1) not adjacent to R(6). Arrangement: S-T-P-Q-U-R. Second from right = position 5 = U.

explanation: R must be at the right end (R=6) because U immediately left of R would put U at position 0 if R=1. So R=6, U=5. P=3, Q=4 (immediately right of P). S and T fill positions 1 and 2. T between S and U (U=5) means S=1, T=2. Final order: S-T-P-Q-U-R. Second from right is position 5 which is U.

explanation_sections.punchline: R must be at the right end (not left) because 'U immediately left of R' would be invalid at position 1; this chains U to position 5, the second from right.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: test both ends for R - R=1 forces U=0 (impossible), so R=6, U=5. P given at 3, Q at 4. Positions 1 and 2 remain for S and T; 'T between S and U' forces S=1, T=2. Verify S not adjacent to R: 1 and 6 are not adjacent. Row: S-T-P-Q-U-R. Second from right = position 5 = U.
explanation_sections.lesson: Use impossibility to fix the end: if one assignment creates an out-of-bounds seat, the other end is forced.
explanation_sections.timing: 80-90 s. Key trap: reading 'second from right' as position 2 from left (giving T or S) instead of position 5.
